author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader narrows the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both forms of the veterinarian directory, the page and the machine-readable list, can be narrowed to the veterinarians holding one named specialty. The name matches in full, letter case is disregarded, and naming no specialty leaves the directory as it is today.
acceptance_criteria: given a specialty held by at least one veterinarian, when the page directory is narrowed to it, then only those veterinarians are listed, a page at a time, and the page count reflects the narrowed directory
given the same specialty, when the machine-readable directory is narrowed to it, then it carries only those veterinarians
given a specialty named in different letter case from the recorded one, when either form is narrowed to it, then the same veterinarians are listed
given the opening letters of a specialty's name rather than the whole name, when either form is narrowed to it, then no veterinarian is listed
given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either form is narrowed to it, then the directory is presented as usual with no veterinarian in it and no failure is reported
given no specialty, or one that is empty or entirely spaces, when either form is requested, then every veterinarian is listed exactly as before this change
given a veterinarian holding more than one specialty, when the directory is narrowed to any one of them, then that veterinarian is listed
given no specialty, when the machine-readable directory is requested, then it carries every veterinarian with the specialties each holds (REQ-VET-003 regression)
non_goals: free-text search for a veterinarian by name (NG-9, narrowed 2026-08-04)
filtering or searching pets and visits (NG-9)
managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2)
narrowing the directory by any attribute other than specialty
notes: REQ-VET-003 reinstates the machine-readable veterinarian list as a supported surface; the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused. REQ-VET-003 needs no new behavior, so its regression is batched into this slice rather than shipped as a slice of its own. Product-owner constraint carried from the elicitation: the request-level selector is named the same on both surfaces and the human fixed that name as 'specialty'; the mechanism is system-design's to record. Deliberately unspecified: whether a non-empty specialty with surrounding spaces is trimmed before matching. Only the empty-or-whitespace-only case is decided (behaves as absent, mirroring owner search). NG-9 narrowing recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-04-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md. The ADR index in docs/adr/README.md needs a row for that ADR; it is outside this agent's write scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty filter extends the vet feature package in place: no new package, no service layer, controller talks to the repository directly, per docs/system-design.md Package Structure and the feature-package ADR. The narrowing itself is new design ground, recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-04-specialty-narrowing-as-a-repository-query.md and reflected in system-design.md Contracts, Persistence, and Threat Model. Three decisions are load-bearing. (1) Narrowing is a repository query, not a controller-side filter over the cached list: the PRD requires narrowing before paging, and the database must count the narrowed rows for totalPages to be right. This also mirrors OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith(lastName, pageable), the project's one existing narrow-and-page precedent, and keeps page arithmetic out of the controller. (2) Case folding happens in the query (Spring Data IgnoreCase, compiling to upper() on both sides), never in the column collation: specialties.name is VARCHAR(80) in H2 and TEXT in PostgreSQL with no case-insensitive typing, so relying on the database would reproduce the recorded owner-search defect where the same search differs per vendor. (3) The narrowed finders carry no @Cacheable, departing from the package's read-caching convention: their key would include a caller-supplied string on a route open to every caller, and the vets cache is declared through JCache with no size limit.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two derived finders over the specialty name: a paged one for /vets.html and an unpaged Collection<Vet> one for /vets. Neither is annotated @Cacheable; findAll() and findAll(Pageable) keep their @Cacheable("vets") unchanged.
Both VetController handlers take @RequestParam(required = false) String specialty. The parameter name 'specialty' is a fixed product-owner constraint and is identical on both routes.

VetController strips the parameter and treats null-or-blank as absent, then calls the unnarrowed finders. Whole-name equality offers no sentinel meaning 'every vet', so this branch cannot move into the query the way the owner search's empty prefix does; the repository never sees a blank specialty.

vetList.html pagination links must carry the active specialty. Every th:href in the pager currently hardcodes '/vets.html?page=N'; dropping the parameter on page 2 would silently un-narrow the directory and contradict the paging acceptance criterion.
The JSON route keeps returning the Vets wrapper; only the collection it wraps is narrowed.

patterns.description: narrow-and-page in one derived repository query, returning Page<T> — the shape the paged specialty finder follows
strip the caller's text and treat the blank case as 'no narrowing' before reaching the repository — the trim rule this slice reuses
existing findPaginated helper (page size 5, PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize)) — the narrowed variant extends this helper rather than adding a second pagination scheme

risks.risk: Case-insensitive matching left to the database would pass on H2 and MySQL and fail on PostgreSQL, repeating the recorded owner-search defect. The H2-backed test suite cannot observe the divergence.
risks.mitigation: Fold case in the query (IgnoreCase / upper()), never in the schema. Do not add a case-insensitive column type or index to any vendor schema for this slice.

risks.risk: The join through vet_specialties returns one row per matching specialty, so a vet holding two specialties recorded under the same name would appear twice and inflate the page count.
risks.mitigation: Use Distinct in the derived method name; Spring Data then also emits count(distinct ...) for the Page count query.

risks.risk: Derived-query property resolution over Vet.specialties may not resolve as expected: the field is Set<Specialty> while the getter returns List<Specialty>, and a protected getSpecialtiesInternal() accessor sits alongside.
risks.mitigation: Verify against a real repository (@DataJpaTest) rather than only through MockMvc with a mocked repository. If resolution misbehaves, fall back to an explicit parameterized @Query in JPQL, which the codebase already permits.

risks.risk: Adding @Cacheable to the narrowed finders would let any unauthenticated caller mint an unbounded number of cache entries keyed by an arbitrary string, in a cache declared with no size limit.
risks.mitigation: Leave the narrowed finders uncached, as decided in the ADR. The pre-existing page-number key on findAll(Pageable) is out of scope for this slice and is now recorded in the Threat Model.

risks.risk: Tests that mock VetRepository can assert the controller's branch but not that the query narrows, folds case, or pages correctly — the acceptance criteria that matter most would be asserted against a double.
risks.mitigation: Cover the whole-name, case-insensitive, prefix-non-match, and no-match criteria at the repository level against the real database; keep MockMvc for the routing, parameter-binding, and model-attribute assertions.

notes: Open question from the PRD dispatch, decided here: a padded non-empty value is stripped before matching, so '?specialty=%20radiology%20' matches 'radiology'. The project already strips caller text in OwnerController before searching, and one strip call yields the decided empty-or-whitespace-only rule as a by-product (strip, then test for empty). No consultation needed. Durable-memory writes accompanying this verdict: new ADR docs/adr/2026-08-04-specialty-narrowing-as-a-repository-query.md; docs/adr/README.md index rows for that ADR and for the product-owned non-goal ADR 2026-08-04-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md; system-design.md Contracts rows for VetRepository, VetController, and Vets (Implements now cites REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004); a Persistence rule that case folding lives in the query with an ADR back-link; a Threat Model row for unbounded cache growth from caller-controlled keys; and removal of the stale Known Defects row claiming the machine-readable vet route serves no requirement and is pending removal — REQ-VET-003 reinstates it as a supported surface. No design-doc-autofix records were present to audit. Vocabulary: the feature is the 'Specialty filter' per docs/ubiquitous-language.md; 'vet search' and 'veterinarian search' are the terms to avoid, and free-text vet search stays out of scope under the narrowed NG-9.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the specialty narrowing is a Spring Data derived query (findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase, VetRepository.java:71 and :83) with the caller value bound as a parameter. No @Query, no JPQL or SQL string, no concatenation anywhere in the diff (swept the whole change set for @Query/createQuery/nativeQuery/string concatenation - zero hits in production code).

Cross-site scripting: the caller-supplied specialty reaches the template only as a link-expression parameter (vetList.html:34,40,46,52,58). Thymeleaf URL-encodes @{} query-parameter values and escapes th:href output; escaping is nowhere disabled - no th:utext, no th:inline, no javascript: or event-handler attribute is introduced. VetControllerTests asserts the encoding directly (specialty=%3Cscript%3E present, specialty=<script> absent), so the property is held by a test and not just by inspection.

Pagination URL injection: verified the value cannot break out of the pager links. The unnarrowed branch omits the parameter entirely rather than emitting an empty one, and the narrowed branch passes specialty through @{} rather than interpolating it into a URL string, so no preconstructed URL text ever concatenates caller input.

Cache-key exposure: confirmed the design block's claim against the code - neither narrowed finder carries @Cacheable, while findAll() and findAll(Pageable) keep theirs unchanged. A caller-supplied string therefore never becomes a key in the size-unlimited JCache-declared vets cache. The pre-existing page-number key on findAll(Pageable) is unchanged by this slice and is recorded in the system-design Threat Model; per docs/security-principles.md it is baseline, not a finding here.

Boundary validation and least privilege: specialtyFilter (VetController.java:83) strips the value and maps null-or-blank to null at the boundary, so the repository never receives a blank filter. Both new finders are @Transactional(readOnly = true) - read-only scope for a read-only feature. No new endpoint, route, or actuator exposure: the two routes already existed and gain one optional query parameter.

Data exposure: the narrowed routes return the same Vet fields the unnarrowed routes already returned - narrowing can only shrink the result set, never widen it. No new PII surface, no logging of the caller value, no exception message carrying it.

Secrets: swept the full change set for credential-shaped strings (password, secret, token, key, credential). The only hit is prose in the system-design Threat Model describing the pre-existing committed defaults. No new credential is introduced in any file.

Supply chain: no dependency change to verify - build.gradle, settings.gradle, and the gradle/ wrapper are untouched by this change set (confirmed via git status), so no new artifact, repository, or framework version enters the build and the existing CVE posture is unchanged.

Whole-name vs. prefix (theSpecialtyFilterShouldNotMatchAPartialSpecialtyName), no-match-yields-empty-200 (theSpecialtyFilterShouldYieldAnEmptyDirectoryWhenNoVetHoldsTheSpecialty / theVetJsonListShouldCarryOnlyVetsHoldingTheGivenSpecialty), blank/whitespace-as-absent (theBlankSpecialtyFilterShouldListEveryVet, theBlankSpecialtyFilterShouldCarryEveryVetInTheJsonList), padding-stripped (thePaddedSpecialtyFilterShouldMatchTheStrippedName), pagination-on-narrowed-set (theVetListPageShouldPaginateTheNarrowedDirectory, theNarrowedPageShouldSpanTheNarrowedDirectoryOnly), pager-carries-specialty (theVetListPagerShouldCarryTheSpecialtyThroughEveryLink), reflected-value HTML-encoding (thePagerShouldEncodeTheSpecialtyItCarries), and the REQ-VET-003 regression (theVetJsonListShouldCarryEveryVetWhenNoSpecialtyIsGiven) all have dedicated tests matching the PRD's acceptance criteria and edge cases.

BDD naming (the{Subject}Should{Outcome}), four-phase spacing, and AssertJ/hamcrest fluent assertions are used consistently in both new/modified files; no mystery literals — seeded specialty names are explained in the VetRepositoryTests class javadoc.

MockMvc plus @MockitoBean VetRepository in VetControllerTests is consistent with brief § Mocking Policy and CLAUDE.md's sanctioned-mock carve-out: the design deliberately pushes case-folding/whole-name/no-match assertions to the real-database repository test and keeps the controller test scoped to routing, parameter binding, and pagination-model wiring.
./gradlew test --tests 'org.springframework.samples.petclinic.vet.*' passes; JaCoCo reports 100% instruction and branch coverage on VetController for this package, well above the 80% brief target.

author: change-grader
summary: narrow the veterinarian directory by specialty

blast_radius.note: Reach is contained to the vet feature package: two derived finders on VetRepository, two handlers in VetController, the pager block of vetList.html, plus six documentation files. No sensitive paths, no schema or config change, and both existing routes gain one optional parameter additively, so the unnarrowed behavior and the two cached findAll methods are untouched.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every production hunk: absent, empty and all-space values collapse through one shared specialtyFilter helper to the pre-existing cached findAll paths, case folding sits in the derived query rather than the column collation, Distinct guards the vet_specialties join fan-out, and all five pager links carry the filter in the narrowed branch and omit the parameter entirely in the unnarrowed one. Nothing does anything the diff and the ADRs do not say.

test_adequacy.note: A new DataJpaTest runs against a real database and pins the query properties the mocks cannot see: whole-name match, case folding, prefix non-match, empty result for an unheld specialty, and page arithmetic over the narrowed set. The MockMvc tests assert rendered pager markup and URL encoding rather than restating the stubs, and the unnarrowed JSON list is pinned as a REQ-VET-003 regression. Untested: the first and previous pager links never render under a filter, and the padded value is exercised only on the HTML route; both share code paths covered elsewhere and both read correct.

reviewer_hedging.note: The engine rated the slice high risk and dispatched the full four-reviewer battery; all four approved with empty findings lists. The test-reviewer's one note is an explicitly non-blocking suggestion for a symmetric JSON-route test, and the strip logic it concerns is the single shared helper both routes call, which I confirmed in the source.

scope_deviation.note: Two things to confirm. The delivered page carries no reader-facing affordance for the filter: no form control, no active-filter indication, no message key, so a reader can only narrow by hand-editing the query string, while the requirement is titled 'Reader narrows the veterinarian directory to one specialty' and its done-when clauses were authored in this same slice in terms a URL parameter alone satisfies. Separately, the slice carries two further product decisions past REQ-VET-004: REQ-VET-003 reinstates the previously withdrawn /vets JSON route as a permanently supported surface, and NG-9 is narrowed in the PRD. Both are recorded with ADRs, and both are durable commitments that outlive this slice.

rationale: The code is clean and the query is pinned against a real database. What wants your eye is what shipped around it: the page offers no way to set the filter, so it is URL-only, and the slice permanently reinstates /vets as a supported API and narrows NG-9. Confirm all three were intended.
